notes: Starting point compiled from public guidance, NOT verified by the AirFrameXR project on this headset (no `verified` entry). AirFrameXR's support for headsets other than the Apple Vision Pro is best effort.

Quest 2, 3 and 3S share this profile except for the panel size (2064 x 2208 per eye here): they all stream HEVC with ALVR's Android client and a Qualcomm Snapdragon XR2 decoder (Quest 3 and 3S: XR2 Gen 2; Quest 2: XR2 Gen 1). Against the Apple Vision Pro profile (3552 x 3200, 300 Mbps, split encoding) the stream has 2-2.4x fewer pixels and needs about half the bitrate. Same as on the Vision Pro: 90 Hz, HEVC 10-bit (the default session forces it; ALVR's Quest client advertises 10-bit support), full colour range; chroma-key passthrough is off by default (the setup offers it, key colour pure green #00FF00). Foveation is ALVR's 'Light' preset (centre 0.80 x 0.80, edge ratio 8 x 8): nearly the whole view stays at full resolution, the saving is small on purpose.

ALVR's wiki (Settings tutorial, v20): on a good wireless router use the medium resolution preset (the default) with sharpening 1.0 and HEVC at a constant 100-150 Mbps; HEVC is usually the best codec when bitrate is limited; turn foveated encoding on and tune it from the statistics graph.
Resolution, gamma and the encoder details are left out on purpose: the headset's own default (what ALVR reports at the handshake) is used. Change them in the wizard if you know better.
Panel about 2064 x 2208 per eye (Meta's specification); refresh rates 72/80/90/120 Hz. 90 Hz is the commonly recommended balance, 72 Hz the stable fallback.
ALVR's wiki: AV1 works only on the Quest 3 with an RTX 4000 / RX 7000 or newer GPU. AirFrameXR's encoder path is HEVC, so this does not apply here.
